issue.title: takeoff_and_landing.cpp won't build.
issue.body:
Copy and pasted takeoff_and_landing.cpp into test.cpp from https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/examples/takeoff_and_land/takeoff_and_land.cpp

```
CMakeLists.txt:
add_executable(test test.cpp)

target_link_libraries(test  
                MAVSDK::mavsdk)
```

```
$ cmake ..
-- Configuring done
-- Generating done
-- Build files have been written to: /home/me/Development/myProject/build

[me@workstation1 build]$ make
[ 25%] Building CXX object src/CMakeFiles/test.dir/test.cpp.o
/home/me/Development/myProject/src/test.cpp: In function ‘std::shared_ptr<mavsdk::System> get_system(mavsdk::Mavsdk&)’:
/home/me/Development/myProject/src/test.cpp:37:13: error: ‘NewSystemHandle’ is not a member of ‘mavsdk::Mavsdk’
   37 |     Mavsdk::NewSystemHandle handle = mavsdk.subscribe_on_new_system([&mavsdk, &prom, &handle]() {
      |             ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/home/me/Development/myProject/src/test.cpp:47:6: error: expected primary-expression before ‘)’ token
   47 |     });
      |      ^
make[2]: *** [src/CMakeFiles/test.dir/build.make:76: src/CMakeFiles/test.dir/test.cpp.o] Error 1
make[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:115: src/CMakeFiles/test.dir/all] Error 2
make: *** [Makefile:91: all] Error 2
```

It can't find NewSystemHandle. 

```
cd /usr/include/mavsdk
grep -r NewSystem
mavsdk.h:    using NewSystemCallback = std::function<void()>;
mavsdk.h:    void subscribe_on_new_system(const NewSystemCallback& callback);
```

comments.body: Which version of MAVSDK are you using with those examples? If you build MAVSDK from sources from branch `main`, then you can use the examples from branch `main`. If you use MAVSDK `v1.4.3`, then you should use the examples from tag `v1.4.3`.

OK, got it working.
The example link I was using pointed to version 1.1 ish code.
My MAVSDK install was version 1.4.3.

On GitHub, the example on the "main" branch still uses the old code.
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/examples/takeoff_and_land/takeoff_and_land.cpp

However, if one selects version 1.4.3, it uses the new code.
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4.3/examples/takeoff_and_land/takeoff_and_land.cpp

Thanks for replying to my posts.

> On GitHub, the example on the "main" branch still uses the old code.

I think there is some confusion here.

* The `main` branch is the development branch. It contains the latest everything (code, examples, etc).
* A release on GitHub is associated to a git [tag](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Tagging), which points the whole repo to a commit in the past.
* As a consequence, `main` keeps evolving, while tags (like `v1.4.3`) will never change.
* In order to make sure that the repo is consistent (the code builds on the supported platforms, the tests passes, and the examples build), we have setup a CI (continuous integration) system [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/.github/workflows/main.yml). This means that for a given branch/tag, the examples should always be compatible with the code (it was verified by the CI).

I am pretty sure that the reason why the examples from `main` don't work when you build against the `v1.4.3` tag is because `main` is _newer_, not older. In fact, the next release coming from `main` will be `v2.0.0`, because (as you realised here) it is breaking the `v1.x.x` API.

Does that help?
Is there still a question, or should we close this issue?

> 
thanks a lot, it may really helps.
Not sure how this is meant to be "fixed"? Examples from `main` branch don't build against the current homebrew install. Is there a correct branch to be using that does build?

What is the current homebrew install, and did you try to build the examples from the corresponding [release tag](https://github.com/mavlink/mavsdk/releases)?

As commented [above](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1843#issuecomment-1176818393), if you try to build an example from `main` (which is going towards v2) against an installation of MAVSDK v1, then probably it will fail (because moving from v1 to v2 means that there are breaking changes in the API).

Does that make sense?

Hi, I did manage to resolve this, so apologies.

Current `homebrew` is at v1.4.7, and the 1.4.7 tag for the repo worked for me. Sorry to bother you!
